name: Vincent O'Sullivan
bio: Writer, and author of Aspects of Wilde (1936), a first-hand memoir of the exile years. Two of Wilde's letters to him survive. In October 1897, while Wilde was at Posillipo with Douglas and being attacked in London, O'Sullivan took his side publicly at the Authors' Club - and Wilde wrote to say he could not express adequately how deeply touched he was.
bio_note: The volume's Index of Recipients. printed 963 carries two letters of the same week, one rebuking [[sherard]] for attacking Wilde behind his back at the Authors' Club, the other thanking o'Sullivan for the position he took there. Two letters at printed 963 and 1160. His memoir is outside this volume and is the obvious next source - he is one of the few witnesses to the last years who wrote at length. Dates not recorded and none inferred.
